summary: A Network Host Status report from Ellen Westheimer of BBN covering March 13 to March 24, 1972. It lists which hosts were left out of daily testing, and notes that the SRI-AI computer became a server during the period. It updates RFC 319. It was replaced by RFC 330.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 326 reports ARPANET host status from March 13 through March 24, 1972. It lists host roles, exclusions from daily tests, and coded test results.

subtitle: A March 1972 report records host status and daily connection tests.

tldr.problem: Network users needed a report of host status and expected availability across the ARPANET.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists host roles and summarizes status tests for March 13 through March 24, including tests from the BBN Terminal IMP.
tldr.outcome: RFC 326 updates RFC 319 and was later obsoleted by RFC 330. The report notes that SRI-AI became a server during the period.

today: RFC 326 updates RFC 319 and was obsoleted by RFC 330. It is a host-status report covering March 13 through March 24, 1972.

sections.title: Report Scope and Host Categories
sections.content: RFC 326 reports on most Network Hosts from March 13 through March 24 and notes that the SRI-AI computer became a server. The document excludes hosts not expected to operate regularly as servers and hosts intended only as users from daily testing.
sections.plainLanguage: The report covers most hosts over a two-week period. It also explains which hosts were not included in the daily tests.

sections.title: The Host Status Tables
sections.content: The RFC includes a table of sites, computers, status predictions, and the people who supplied the information. It also gives test results over ten dates. The status codes include Open, Dead, Refused, Timed Out, and 1/2 Open, where a host opened a connection but closed it or stopped responding.
sections.plainLanguage: One table lists what each host was expected to do. Another records whether test connections opened, failed, timed out, or stopped responding.

sections.title: Updates and Replacement
sections.content: The RFC header says it updates RFC 319. The unit metadata records RFC 330 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 326. This report is a dated snapshot of network host status.
sections.plainLanguage: RFC 326 updates an earlier status report and was itself later replaced. It records one period, rather than a permanent host status.
